technical_and_design_decisions: The codebase is assumed to be a multi-module Maven/Gradle project with Java (Spring Boot) backend and JavaScript/TypeScript frontend (admin-ui, Flo).
Lattice upgrade to 0.6.0 is treated as a minor version upgrade; only dependency updates and minor API adaptations are expected.

Terminology replacements (Spring XD -> Spring Cloud Data Flow, Job(s) -> Task(s)) are performed via global search-and-replace across all source files, including documentation, comments, and configuration, with manual verification to avoid breaking changes.
Consistent look and feel between admin-ui and Flo will be achieved by extracting a shared UI theme library (CSS variables, common components) and applying it to both applications.
The admin-ui about section will be extended by exposing version and SPI type from the backend via an existing or new REST endpoint, and the frontend will consume and display these values.

Flo Graphs screenshots will be generated using a headless browser automation tool (e.g., Puppeteer) integrated into the documentation build pipeline, ensuring screenshots are updated with each release.
Design review will be a time-boxed technical spike producing a written report of known limitations and gaps, not a full redesign.

Shell commands for scaling module instances will be implemented using Spring Shell, leveraging the existing SCDF REST API for scaling operations, and will follow the established command pattern in the shell module.
assumptions: The development team is familiar with the Spring Cloud Data Flow codebase and its modules.
The Lattice 0.6.0 release has no major breaking changes that would require significant refactoring.
All terminology replacements are limited to references (strings, documentation, UI labels) and do not require changes to core domain model class names or database schemas.
The admin-ui and Flo are separate frontend applications but can share a common UI library via a private npm package or shared source folder.
The backend already exposes version information; SPI type exposure may require a small addition to an existing endpoint.
Batch DSL documentation is written in AsciiDoc or Markdown and can embed images.
The design review activity is limited to 2 days (16 hours) and focuses on identification only, not implementation of fixes.
Testing effort is estimated at roughly 30% of the total development effort for the user stories.
Documentation updates for U2, U3, U5, U8 are separate from the Flo Graphs screenshots (U6).
Code review and merge overhead is estimated at 2 days (16 hours) for the entire increment.
Build and release preparation includes updating changelogs, version numbers, and running the release build.
